scales.name: How sweet?
scales.question: Sweetness compared with table sugar (sugar = 1). Each gridline step is ten times sweeter.

measure.words: times as sweet as the same amount of table sugar (sugar = 1)
measure.origin: There's no machine for sweetness: it's measured by tasting panels comparing a substance with table sugar.

items.name: Lugduname
items.fact: Lugduname is one of the sweetest substances known; it has never been approved as food.

items.name: Cyclamate
items.fact: Cyclamate was discovered in 1937 by a student who noticed his cigarette tasted sweet.

items.name: Neotame
items.fact: Neotame is a close relative of aspartame, about 40 times sweeter.

items.name: Table sugar (sucrose)
items.fact: Sucrose is the yardstick: everything else is measured against it.

items.name: Saccharin
items.fact: Saccharin, from 1879, is the oldest artificial sweetener.

scales.name: Country size
scales.question: Land and water area in square kilometers. Each gridline step is ten times bigger.

measure.words: square kilometres of land and water
measure.origin: Square kilometres are the standard for country sizes. Vatican City would fit into New York's Central Park more than seven times.

items.name: Luxembourg
items.fact: Luxembourg is the #170 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Japan
items.fact: Japan is the #65 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Vatican City
items.fact: Vatican City is the #197 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Russia
items.fact: Russia is the #1 largest of 197 countries by area.

items.name: Nauru
items.fact: Nauru is the #195 largest of 197 countries by area.

scales.name: Melting point
scales.question: The temperature where each one turns to liquid.

measure.words: degrees Celsius at which it melts
measure.origin: Scientists often use kelvin instead: add 273.15 to degrees Celsius, so the scale starts at absolute zero.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, which made it ideal for light-bulb filaments.

items.name: Copper
items.fact: Copper melts only about 20 °C above gold.

items.name: Platinum
items.fact: Platinum is denser than gold.

items.name: Cocoa butter (chocolate)
items.fact: Chocolate is designed to melt just below body temperature.

items.name: Aluminium
items.fact: Aluminium was once more valuable than gold.

scales.name: When was it completed?
scales.question: The year each landmark was finished or opened.

measure.words: the year it was finished or opened
measure.origin: Counting years from the birth of Jesus was worked out by the monk Dionysius Exiguus in the year 525.

items.name: Big Ben (Elizabeth Tower)
items.fact: Big Ben's bell cracked shortly after it first rang.

items.name: St. Peter's Basilica
items.fact: Michelangelo designed St. Peter's dome.

items.name: Westminster Hall
items.fact: Westminster Hall is the oldest part of the Houses of Parliament.

items.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
items.fact: The current Golden Pavilion is a 1955 rebuild after an arson attack.

items.name: Burj Khalifa
items.fact: The Burj Khalifa has 163 floors.

scales.name: Running time
scales.question: How long each film is, in minutes.

measure.words: minutes from opening to end credits
measure.origin: For the Oscars, a film has to run longer than 40 minutes to count as a feature film.

items.name: Inception (2010)
items.fact: Many effects in Inception were done for real, including the rotating hallway.

items.name: Barbie (2023)
items.fact: Barbie was the highest-grossing film of 2023.

items.name: Toy Story (1995)
items.fact: Toy Story was the first entirely computer-animated feature film.

items.name: Lawrence of Arabia (1962)
items.fact: Lawrence of Arabia has no speaking roles for women.

items.name: Oppenheimer (2023)
items.fact: Oppenheimer won seven Oscars including Best Picture.

scales.name: Density
scales.question: Kilograms per cubic meter (water is 1,000). Each gridline step is ten times denser.

measure.words: kilograms in one cubic metre (water = 1,000)
measure.origin: Legend says Archimedes used density to check whether a king's crown was pure gold, and shouted 'Eureka!'.

items.name: Lithium
items.fact: Lithium is the least dense metal; it floats on water.

items.name: Gold
items.fact: A gold bar the size of a milk carton would weigh about 19 kg.

items.name: Air at sea level
items.fact: A cubic meter of air weighs about as much as a bag of sugar.

items.name: Tungsten hexafluoride (a very heavy gas)
items.fact: Tungsten hexafluoride is one of the heaviest gases known, about 10 times denser than air.

items.name: Helium gas
items.fact: Helium balloons float because helium is about 7 times lighter than air.

scales.name: Lifespan
scales.question: Typical (or record) life length, from hours to millennia.

measure.words: typical or record life length, in hours, days or years
measure.origin: Tree ages are counted from growth rings; fish ages from similar rings in their ear bones.

items.name: Adult mayfly
items.fact: Adult mayflies have no working mouths; they live only to mate.

items.name: Golden hamster
items.fact: Almost all pet hamsters descend from a few hamsters caught in Syria in 1930.

items.name: Fruit fly
items.fact: Fruit flies are one of the most studied animals in genetics.

items.name: Ocean quahog clam (record)
items.fact: The record clam, nicknamed Ming, was born in the 1490s.

items.name: Horse
items.fact: A horse's age can be estimated from its teeth.

scales.name: Mohs hardness
scales.question: Which scratches which? 1 is soft as talc, 10 is diamond.

measure.words: which mineral scratches which: 1 is talc, 10 is diamond
measure.origin: Devised in 1812 by German geologist Friedrich Mohs. Field geologists still carry little scratch kits to use it.

items.name: Potassium metal
items.fact: Potassium is soft enough to cut with a butter knife.

items.name: Topaz
items.fact: Pure topaz is colorless; most blue topaz in shops has been treated.

items.name: Apatite
items.fact: The enamel on your teeth is mostly a form of apatite.

items.name: Calcite
items.fact: Calcite makes up limestone and marble.

items.name: Diamond
items.fact: One step above corundum, but about four times as hard.

scales.name: Loudness
scales.question: Sound pressure level in decibels. Every +10 dB sounds roughly twice as loud.

measure.words: decibels of sound pressure: +10 dB sounds about twice as loud
measure.origin: The 'bel' is named after telephone inventor Alexander Graham Bell. Engineers at Bell Labs introduced it in the 1920s.

items.name: Chainsaw (1 m)
items.fact: Chainsaw operators are required to wear ear protection.

items.name: Television
items.fact: The US EPA names 75 dB as the level to stay under to protect your hearing.

items.name: A very calm room
items.fact: A quiet bedroom at night is around 25 dB.

items.name: Quietest room on Earth (Microsoft's anechoic chamber)
items.fact: Decibels can go below zero: zero is only the faintest sound a typical ear can hear.

items.name: Jet engine (1 m)
items.fact: Airport ground crew wear heavy ear defenders for good reason.

scales.name: Boiling point
scales.question: The temperature where each one boils, at normal air pressure.

measure.words: degrees Celsius at which it boils, at sea-level air pressure
measure.origin: Anders Celsius's original 1742 scale was upside down: 0 was boiling water and 100 was freezing. It was flipped after his death.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten boils at about the temperature of the Sun's surface.

items.name: Sodium
items.fact: Sodium-vapor street lamps glow orange.

items.name: Lead
items.fact: Lead boils at a temperature hotter than lava from many volcanoes.

items.name: Nitrogen
items.fact: Liquid nitrogen is used to make 'instant' ice cream.

items.name: Copper
items.fact: Copper vapor lasers produce yellow and green light.

scales.name: Voltage
scales.question: How much electrical tension? Each gridline step is ten times more.

measure.words: volts of electrical tension
measure.origin: Named after Italian physicist Alessandro Volta, who built the first battery in 1800.

items.name: Nerve cell at rest
items.fact: Every nerve cell is a tiny battery, kept charged by pumping ions.

items.name: Lightning bolt
items.fact: A typical lightning bolt spans about 100 million volts end to end.

items.name: Electric fence
items.fact: Electric fences use high voltage but very short, low-current pulses.

items.name: Brain waves (EEG) at the scalp
items.fact: Brain waves are measured in millionths of a volt.

items.name: Car battery
items.fact: A car battery has six cells of about 2 volts each.

scales.name: Energy density
scales.question: Calories (kcal) in 100 grams of each.

measure.words: kilocalories in 100 grams of the food
measure.origin: A food 'Calorie' is really a kilocalorie: the energy needed to warm 1 kg of water by 1 °C.

items.name: Honey
items.fact: Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was still edible.

items.name: Cucumber
items.fact: Cucumbers are about 95% water.

items.name: Almonds
items.fact: Almonds are seeds, not true nuts.

items.name: Olive oil
items.fact: Oil is pure fat, the most energy-dense nutrient.

items.name: Butter
items.fact: Butter is about 80% fat.

scales.name: Radiation dose
scales.question: Effective dose in sieverts (Sv). Each gridline step is ten times more.

measure.words: sieverts of effective dose (1 mSv = a thousandth of a sievert)
measure.origin: Named after Swedish medical physicist Rolf Sievert, a pioneer of radiation protection.

items.name: Dental X-rays
items.fact: A set of dental X-rays is about the same as a day of natural background radiation.

items.name: Eating a banana
items.fact: Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium-40.

items.name: Six months on the Space Station
items.fact: Astronauts get about 80 mSv in six months on the ISS.

items.name: Dose fatal to half of people (short exposure)
items.fact: Doses spread out over time are far less harmful than the same dose all at once.

items.name: Mammogram
items.fact: Mammograms use low-energy X-rays.

scales.name: How much does the sting hurt?
scales.question: Schmidt sting pain index: entomologist Justin Schmidt rated the pain of insect stings he received, from 1 (mild) to 4 (excruciating).

measure.words: Schmidt sting pain index: 1 is mild, 4 is excruciating
measure.origin: Entomologist Justin Schmidt built the index from stings he collected while studying insects. His book about it is called The Sting of the Wild.

items.name: Bumble bee
items.fact: Schmidt: "Colorful flames. Fireworks land on your arm."

items.name: Bullet ant
items.fact: Schmidt: "Like walking over flaming charcoal with a 3-inch nail embedded in your heel."

items.name: Paper wasp
items.fact: Schmidt: "A single drop of superheated frying oil landed on your arm."

items.name: Mud dauber wasp
items.fact: Schmidt: "Jalapeño cheese when you were expecting Havarti."

items.name: Nocturnal hornet
items.fact: This hornet hunts at night.

scales.name: How heavy?
scales.question: Mass, from milligrams to millions of tonnes. Each gridline step is ten times heavier.

measure.words: mass in kilograms (1 tonne = 1,000 kg)
measure.origin: From 1889 to 2019 the kilogram was defined by a metal cylinder kept in a vault near Paris.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
items.fact: The Great Pyramid is made of about 2.3 million blocks.

items.name: Grand piano
items.fact: A concert grand weighs about as much as five adults.

items.name: One-euro coin
items.fact: A one-euro coin is made of two different metal alloys.

items.name: Mosquito
items.fact: Smaller mosquito species weigh about 2.5 milligrams.

items.name: International Space Station
items.fact: The ISS was assembled in orbit from dozens of launches.

scales.name: Caffeine
scales.question: Milligrams of caffeine per serving.

measure.words: milligrams of caffeine in one serving
measure.origin: Food-safety agencies such as the EU's EFSA say up to 400 mg a day is fine for most healthy adults.

items.name: Drip coffee (207 ml)
items.fact: Filter coffee is one of the strongest everyday caffeine sources.

items.name: Milk chocolate (100 g)
items.fact: Chocolate also contains theobromine, a milder relative of caffeine.

items.name: Extra-strength caffeine tablet
items.fact: Healthy adults are advised to stay under about 400 mg a day.

items.name: Excedrin painkiller tablet
items.fact: Caffeine makes some painkillers work better.

items.name: Jolt Cola (695 ml)
items.fact: Jolt's 1980s slogan was 'All the sugar and twice the caffeine'.

scales.name: Earthquake magnitude
scales.question: Moment magnitude. Each whole step releases about 32 times more energy.

measure.words: moment magnitude: each whole step releases about 32× more energy
measure.origin: Introduced in 1979 by seismologists Thomas Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori. It replaced the Richter scale for big quakes.

items.name: Christchurch, 2011
items.fact: The Christchurch quake was shallow and very close to the city.

items.name: Kobe, 1995
items.fact: The Kobe earthquake destroyed much of the city's port.

items.name: Mexico City, 1985
items.fact: Mexico City's soft lakebed soil amplified the shaking.

items.name: Tōhoku, Japan, 2011
items.fact: The Tōhoku quake moved Japan's main island about 2.4 m east.

items.name: Valdivia, Chile, 1960
items.fact: Valdivia is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded.

scales.name: How tall
scales.question: Height from base to top, in meters. Each gridline step is ten times taller.

measure.words: metres from base to top
measure.origin: The metre was first defined in 1793 as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the Equator.

items.name: CN Tower
items.fact: The CN Tower was the world's tallest free-standing structure for 31 years.

items.name: Olympus Mons, Mars
items.fact: Olympus Mons is about two and a half times as high as Everest.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza (original)
items.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure for almost 4,000 years.

items.name: Christ the Redeemer statue
items.fact: The statue is struck by lightning several times a year.

items.name: Mount Fuji
items.fact: Mount Fuji last erupted in 1707.

scales.name: pH
scales.question: How acidic or basic is it? 7 is neutral; every step down is ten times more acidic.

measure.words: acidity: 7 is neutral, each step down is 10× more acidic
measure.origin: Introduced in 1909 by Danish chemist Søren Sørensen at the Carlsberg Laboratory, the research lab of the beer brewery.

items.name: Lye (drain cleaner)
items.fact: Lye has been used for centuries to make soap.

items.name: Human blood
items.fact: Blood pH outside about 7.35–7.45 is a medical emergency.

items.name: Lemon juice
items.fact: Lemon juice is 5–6% citric acid.

items.name: Black coffee
items.fact: Dark roasts are usually slightly less acidic than light roasts.

items.name: Household ammonia
items.fact: Never mix ammonia with bleach: together they release toxic gas.

scales.name: How fast?
scales.question: Top or typical speed in km/h. Each gridline step is ten times faster.

measure.words: kilometres per hour
measure.origin: Most countries use km/h on road signs; the UK and US still use miles per hour (1 mph is about 1.6 km/h).

items.name: Earth orbiting the Sun
items.fact: You're moving around the Sun at about 30 km every second.

items.name: Average walking speed
items.fact: Above about 7 km/h it becomes more efficient to run than to walk.

items.name: Airliner cruising
items.fact: An Airbus A380 cruises at about 900 km/h.

items.name: World's fastest snail (record)
items.fact: The record snail covered 33 cm in 2 minutes.

items.name: Light
items.fact: Nothing travels faster than light in a vacuum.

scales.name: How deep down
scales.question: Meters below the water surface. Each gridline step is ten times deeper.

measure.words: metres below the water surface
measure.origin: Sailors measured depth in fathoms: 6 feet (about 1.8 m), roughly the span of a person's outstretched arms.

items.name: Recreational scuba limit
items.fact: Below about 30 m, nitrogen starts to make divers feel drunk.

items.name: Challenger Deep
items.fact: The pressure in Challenger Deep is over 1,000 times that at the surface.

items.name: Where sunlight fades out
items.fact: Below about 200 m there isn't enough light for photosynthesis.

items.name: Emperor penguin dive
items.fact: Emperor penguins can hold their breath for over 20 minutes.

items.name: Average ocean depth
items.fact: The average ocean is deeper than most mountains on land are tall.
